alignments.note: Finite verb with its subject pronoun.
The verb is recast as a light verb plus complement, *will it be advantage*; rule 44 heads it on the complement, and the dummy *it* is the construction's under rule 17.
Supplied *And* for a clause with no conjunction morpheme; rule 14's closing sentence, with the ASV italic corroborating under rule 7.
Light verb plus complement, *shall I have profit*; headed on *profit* under rule 44.
Comparative `מִן` → *more than*, headed on *than* under rule 24.

The ASV recasts the single nominal `חַטָּאת` as a clause *if I had sinned*; the supplied subordinator and verb belong to that noun's own recasting under rule 46's closing paragraph, headed on the word carrying the lexeme. Unit discontinuous around the suffix's *I* under rule 25.
The suffix is the subject of the recast clause and takes the *I* written for it under rule 18.

review_notes: The alternative on the last clause leaves *if* `added` under rule 55; it is not taken because no Hebrew clause stands there for the word to subordinate — the whole clause is the ASV's recasting of one noun, which rule 46's closing paragraph keeps with that noun.
